description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/cartesian_uniform_1d/rules/varcoeff_laplacian_zero_flux_bc (conservative finite-volume variable-coefficient Laplacian div(k grad u), arithmetic-mean faces, zero-flux walls) driven by problems/heat_1d_varcoeff_zero_flux.esm. The problem is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4) — no per-resolution fixture files exist or are needed. The manufactured solution exp(-pi^2 t) cos(pi x) with the closed-form MMS forcing S(x,t) = exp(-pi^2 t) 0.25 pi^2 (3 cos 3 pi x - cos pi x) makes u exact for the continuous variable-coefficient PDE (derivation in the problem file); the recorded relative-L2 and Linf errors at t=0.1 are pure spatial-discretization error, expected to fall as O(dx^2). Unlike the nonuniform zero-flux sibling (whose wall Linf lags), the uniform-grid faces give clean 2nd order in BOTH norms.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

python._doc: LSODA at 1e-12/1e-14 keeps Python temporal truncation negligible against the spatial goldens on the stiff variable-coefficient heat sweep, matching the constant-coefficient heat_1d_zero_grad pinning.

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Rust hangs at every tolerance tried (loosest reltol 1e-6; all three solvers Erk/Bdf/Sdirk wedge). earthsci-toolkit-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this stiff / non-smooth-min-max / large-AST RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard.
